comments.note: Developer's handoff noted 13 LibraryScannerTests; the actual file contains 11 executable test methods. AC #8 (structural: no Task.Run in LibraryScanner) is represented only as a code-review comment in the file — no runnable test. This is acceptable given it is a structural assertion, but a Roslyn analyzer rule or a source-text assertion test would make it machine-verifiable.

BlockingFakeScanner.Complete() calls _proceed.TrySetResult() on a TCS that was completed in the previous run (after StartRefreshAsync_AfterPreviousRun). The TCS is not reset between runs. For the double-run test this works because the second call to StartRefreshAsync uses the same orchestrator and the same already-completed TCS, so WaitAsync returns immediately. If RefreshOrchestratorTests is extended to test multi-cycle behavior, the fake will need a TCS reset in a helper method.
No observation — tests are clean, deterministic, and well-structured with clear AC section headers.

comments.note: No blocking issues found — code is clean, deterministic, and well-structured.

[documentation-forward] ILibraryScanner.RefreshAsync (src/VideoIndexer.Core/Abstractions/ILibraryScanner.cs) documents the cooperative-cancellation contract but is silent on the threading contract: implementations must NOT use Task.Run or Thread internally — scheduling is the RefreshOrchestrator's responsibility. This constraint is documented on the concrete LibraryScanner class XML comment but not on the interface. Add a remarks paragraph to the interface so future implementors know they must not spin up background threads.

BlockingFakeScanner in RefreshOrchestratorTests.cs uses a single TaskCompletionSource _proceed that is not reset between runs. The second-run test (StartRefreshAsync_AfterPreviousRun_DoesNotThrow) works correctly because WaitAsync on an already-completed TCS returns immediately. However, if future tests need to exercise multi-cycle behaviour with a blocking second run, the fake will need a Reset() helper that replaces _proceed with a new TCS. The limitation is clearly noted in the test comment — no action needed now.

AC-8 structural assertion (no Task.Run in LibraryScanner) is represented only as a code-review comment in LibraryScannerTests.cs. The constraint is validated by code review rather than a runnable test. A Roslyn analyzer rule (e.g., banning Task.Run within a specific namespace) would make this machine-verifiable, but is out of scope for this WP.
